subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should #35203 remain a core/API design track for missing multi-agent seams, or should most of the proposed collaboration stack be redirected to plugins/ClawHub with only narrow core hooks?
rationale: The RFC crosses core agent routing, plugin APIs, shared state storage, memory visibility, config, cost governance, and security boundaries, so automation cannot choose the permanent product boundary safely.

options.title: Keep canonical RFC, split phases
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and require smaller reviewed issues or PRs for each layer with explicit security and storage decisions.

options.title: Core seams only, plugins own features
options.body: Narrow this issue to missing plugin/API seams and redirect blackboard, dashboards, and orchestration policy to ClawHub-hosted plugins.

options.title: Close as out of scope
options.body: Close the RFC if maintainers decide heavy multi-agent collaboration is not an OpenClaw core priority even as a design discussion.

recommendation.title: Keep canonical RFC, split phases
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical design item and require smaller reviewed issues or PRs for each layer with explicit security and storage decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current scoping signal across related orchestration issues and recent work on the implicated subagent/session/usage surfaces.
